prefixManager_explainerBefore: A prefix is a self-contained, virtual Windows filesystem — with its own
prefixManager_explainerAfter: and its own registry — for installed programs. Every prefix is completely separate from your actual Linux system and from other prefixes, like its own small Windows install just for this one game.
prefixManager_hint: A new, empty folder or an already existing Wine prefix (e.g. from PortProton, Lutris, or Bottles) — it's initialized automatically the first time the game launches, with the runner you choose for this game.
prefixManager_usedByAfter: These games keep the prefix even if it's only removed from Prefixr.
prefixManager_deleteExplain: The prefix is only removed from Prefixr. The directory on disk, installed programs, and saves inside it stay untouched.
runnerList_explainerBefore: A runner is the compatibility layer that gets a Windows game running on Linux at all — e.g.
runnerList_explainerAfter: It translates the game's Windows calls into the Linux system, essentially a translation layer between the two worlds.

wineTools_cmd_description: Open a Windows command line in this prefix.

wineTools_taskmgr_description: View and end running Windows processes in this prefix.

winetricksVerbs_vcrun2022_description: Covers most modern games reporting a missing MSVCP/VCRUNTIME DLL.
winetricksVerbs_vcrun2013_description: For titles from around 2013-2015 that still expect the old msvcr120/msvcp120.
winetricksVerbs_dotnet48_description: For launchers or games whose installer/UI is itself written in .NET.
winetricksVerbs_corefonts_description: Arial, Times New Roman & co. — fixes missing or wrongly rendered text.
winetricksVerbs_d3dcompiler_47_descripti: d3dcompiler_47.dll — often missing on DirectX 9-to-11 titles.
winetricksVerbs_d3dx9_description: Broader than d3dcompiler_47 — for older DirectX 9 titles expecting the full D3DX9 DLL.
winetricksVerbs_xact_description: Fixes missing or silent audio in older DirectX games.
winetricksVerbs_quartz_description: For video cutscenes in older titles that would otherwise stay black or crash.
winetricksVerbs_physx_description: For older games with Nvidia PhysX effects that expect the library explicitly.
winetricksVerbs_gdiplus_description: For older game UIs/launchers built on Microsoft's GDI+ graphics library.
winetricksVerbs_vb6run_description: For very old game installers/launchers still written in VB6.
winetricksInstaller_hintBefore: Installs Windows dependencies directly into this prefix (
winetricksInstaller_hintAfter: ) — affects every game that uses it. Depending on the selection this can take several minutes, since the original files are downloaded from each vendor. A ✓ marks packages already installed.
performanceSettings_mapCountWarningBody: Currently {current}, recommended at least {recommended}. Several modern games (including those with Easy Anti-Cheat, Elden Ring, Baldur's Gate 3, Diablo IV) crash right on launch below this. Steam sets this value itself system-wide — games outside Steam don't get it without this fix.
performanceSettings_hint: How the system treats a running game. Applies to all games and can be overridden per game (edit game → Performance). Each one requires the underlying tool to be installed.
performanceEditor_gamemode_enabled_descr: Optimizes CPU clock and priority while the game runs.
performanceEditor_gamemode_enabled_info: Recommendation: if installed, safe to enable — often gives a noticeable performance boost, especially on laptops or with power saving active. No downside if GameMode is missing. If a competing scheduler daemon is already running (e.g. ananicy-cpp, scx), GameMode is automatically skipped and the performance power profile is used instead, to avoid CPU-priority conflicts.
performanceEditor_power_profile_enabled_: Keeps the power profile on “Performance” while a game runs.

Recommendation: practically always useful on laptops, usually has no effect on desktops without power profiles. Complements GameMode rather than replacing it — GameMode sets the CPU governor itself, which the power-profile service on many distros overrides again. Needs power-profiles-daemon; without it, nothing happens.
performanceEditor_inhibit_sleep_enabled_: Keeps the system and screen awake while a game runs.
Recommendation: practically always useful — stops the screensaver or power saving from kicking in mid-game. Needs systemd-inhibit; without it, nothing happens.
graphicsSettings_hint: What happens to the game's picture before it reaches the screen. Applies to all games and can be overridden per game (edit game → Graphics).
graphicsEditor_gamescopeDescription: Launches the game in its own, nested compositor session.
graphicsEditor_gamescopeInfo: Recommendation: for handhelds/TV setups, or to force resolution and FPS limit independent of the game. Needs the gamescope package; without it, nothing happens. Skipped when Prefixr itself is already running inside a Gamescope session.
graphicsEditor_vkbasaltInfo: Recommendation: always costs some performance (extra post-processing step) — only enable if you have GPU headroom to spare and care more about the visual result than the last few FPS.
graphicsEditor_sharpenInfo: Recommendation: barely any performance hit — especially worthwhile with upscaling or a lower resolution, to regain sharpness.
graphicsEditor_smaaInfo: Recommendation: can cause a noticeable performance hit. If the game already has its own anti-aliasing, better to leave this off — otherwise it just costs extra performance.
overlaySettings_hint: The MangoHud in-game overlay. On/off and appearance apply to all games and can be overridden per game (edit game → Overlay).
mangohud_presets_minimal_description: Just the FPS number, tucked in the corner.
mangohud_presets_standard_description: FPS, usage, and temperatures at a glance.
mangohud_presets_detailed_description: Every value, including status icons and technical info.
mangohud_presets_competitive_description: Big, bold, nothing else — for maximum clarity.
overlayEditor_mangohudDescription: Shows FPS, usage, and temperatures directly in the game. Requires MangoHud to be installed.
protonSettings_hint: Switches that Proton itself evaluates. Apply to all games with a Proton runner and can be overridden per game (edit game → Proton). “Default” leaves the decision to Proton and protonfixes.
protonSettings_noRunner: No Proton runner installed yet — download one first under “Runners”.
protonOptions_hdr_description: Outputs HDR when the monitor and desktop support it. Usually also needs the Wayland driver or Gamescope.
protonOptions_wayland_description: Native Wayland driver instead of XWayland. Can improve latency and scaling.
protonOptions_wined3d_description: For old DirectX 8/9 games that show graphical glitches or won't start with DXVK.
protonOptions_dlss_description: Replaces the game's DLSS version with the latest. Nvidia only.
protonOptions_fsr4_description: Upgrades FSR 3.1 in the game to FSR 4. AMD RDNA4 only.
protonOptions_fsr4rdna3_description: Like “Update FSR 4”, but with the variant for RDNA3 cards.
protonOptions_xess_description: Replaces the game's XeSS version with the latest.
protonOptions_disablenvapi_description: Turns off DLSS/Reflex support. Helps when a game crashes due to Nvidia detection.
protonOptions_forcenvapi_description: Presents even AMD cards as an Nvidia GPU with NVAPI. For games that otherwise hide DLSS/Reflex options.
protonOptions_nontsync_description: Only for hangs or crashes related to NTSync.
protonOptions_nofsync_description: Only for hangs or crashes related to Fsync.
protonOptions_localshadercache_descripti: Creates the shader cache per game instead of sharing it with other games.
protonOptions_forcelgadd_description: Sets the Large-Address-Aware flag. Helps old, heavily modded games against out-of-memory crashes.
protonOptions_sdlinput_description: Reads controllers via SDL instead of Steam Input.
protonEditor_advancedHint: Other switches from the runner's script, without a description. Only change these if a fix for a game specifically calls for it.
protonEditor_unsetKnownHint: Set, but not recognized by the runner:
githubSettings_hint: The list here calls the GitHub API, which without sign-in only allows 60 requests per hour and then responds with a 403 error. A free personal access token (with no permissions at all, just "Public Repositories") raises the limit to 5000 requests per hour. Create one at github.com/settings/tokens?type=beta and paste it here.
steamGridDbSettings_hint: To fetch cover art for the library, a free SteamGridDB API key is needed. Create one at steamgriddb.com/profile/preferences/api and paste it here.
umuSettings_hintBefore: Runs Proton runners through umu — the same way Steam itself launches Proton: in the Steam Linux Runtime, with all
umuSettings_hintAfter: options and automatic per-game fixes (protonfixes). umu loads automatically the first time a Proton game launches; the Steam Runtime (a few hundred MB) too, once, and is shared with Lutris, Heroic & co.
